We present a new deep learning architecture for audiovisual speech recognition, which combines residual networks and bidirectional LSTMs, and attains 11% misclassification rate for lipreading and 4% for audiovisual speech.
The main takeaway from our work is that

deep learning architectures can be successfully used for audiovisual speech recognition and that the visual modality provides useful information for the recognition of difficult words, especially when the acoustic signal is corrupted by noise.
deep networks are capable of learning the temporal and linguistic structure of the audiovisual input and can thus be used to improve audiovisual word recognition.
